ROLL CALL: At 6:19 p.m., on Monday, July 24, 2023, the Alhambra City Council met in the Council
Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MAZA, MALONEY, PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER
ABSENT:

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledged that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

4.  UPDATE FROM THE SAN GABRIEL VALLEY MOSQUITO & VECTOR CONTROL
  DISTRICT – F2M4-46

  Mr. Jason Farned, District Manager for the San Gabriel Valley Mosquito & Vector Control

5.  CONSIDERATION OF AN URGENCY ORDINANCE, ENACTED PURSUANT TO
  GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 65858, PLACING A TEMPORARY MORATORIUM ON
  THE ISSUANCE OF PERMITS OR ENTITLEMENTS FOR ANY SELF-STORAGE PROJECT
  IN THE CITY – F2M23-7, O2M23-4816

  City Attorney MONTES delivered a staff report. At the June 26, 2023 City Council meeting,
  the City Council gave direction to agendize consideration of a moratorium ordinance that would
  prohibit the approval of self-storage facilities in the City. Government Code section 65858
  allows for adoption by urgency ordinance of temporary zoning restrictions to preserve the
  health, safety and welfare of residents while more permanent regulation is being developed.
  Per that code section, the initial temporary restriction lasts no longer than 45 days. The
  extension of the 45-day ordinance and subsequent extensions require a public hearing. During
  the effective period of an interim zoning ordinance, the City cannot approve projects that
  violate the ordinance, although the City is still required to process applications during the
  period of the ordinance. The proposed ordinance will preserve the status quo and enable City
  staff to further study the need for and impact from self-storage businesses and allow the staff
  to return to the Council with options for additional regulation of such businesses. Staff is also
  seeking direction from the City Council on language in the proposed draft ordinance;
  specifically, as to whether or not to exempt the two completed applications for new self-storage
  facilities from the scope of the ordinance.

  Public Comment:

  The following individual expressed their opposition to the proposed ordinance:

  3
7-24-23
   1)  Chris Callahan, Johnson Development Associates
  2)  Alex DeGood, Johnson Development Associates
  3)  Edward Casey, 333 S. Hope Street, Los Angeles
  4)  John Laray, Ray Self Storage

  5) Bert Ng, 203 S. Cordova St., stated the City did not need any additional self-storage
  buildings and expressed support for the proposed ordinance.

  6) Jennifer Ng, S. Cordova St., expressed support for the proposed ordinance.

  7) Lewis McCammon, 105 N. Cordova St., discussed several types of businesses that tend
  to repeat themselves in the City and suggested taking a step back and reexamining what
  types of businesses are being approved.

  Public Comment via Email:

  The following emailed public comments expressed their opposition to the proposed ordinance:

  1) Chris Callahan, Johnson Development Associates
  2) Markie Nevill, three6ixty
  3) Alex DeGood, Cox Castle

  Discussion: Councilmember MALONEY noted that Alhambra is a small town that is
  completely built out, discussed the City’s housing needs, stated that self-storage businesses
  do not bring in sales tax or employ many individuals, and expressed support for the
  moratorium.

  Councilmember PÉREZ noted that this ordinance is about being thoughtful on how the Council
  designs the City and expressed concern with repeat businesses in the City.

  Vice Mayor MAZA discussed the need to give the community different economic development
  opportunities in the City and noted that the two pending projects for self-storage businesses
  should be exempt from the proposed ordinance.

  Councilmember LEE noted that the City has limited vacant land left and needs to be thoughtful
  of what is approved to fill those spaces, discussed the progress of the two pending self-storage
  projects, and noted that the City should stand by the approval for those projects.

  Councilmember MALONEY inquired about the pending projects for self-storage and if the
  proposed project land is contaminated. Director of Community Development HO responded to
  questions.

  Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER expressed concerns with the number of repeat businesses in
  the City and businesses located on contaminated land, expressed support for the moratorium
  but noted that the City should follow through with businesses that have already started the
  process for self-storage businesses in the City.

  Councilmember PÉREZ inquired if staff could begin updating the zoning code while this
  moratorium is in place to not allow self-storage facilities in areas that are not contaminated.
  City Attorney MONTES responded to questions.

  Action Taken:  City Council:

  1.  Found that the recommended action is exempt from the California Environmental
  Quality Act ("CEQA") as set forth in the attached Urgency Ordinance; and,

  4
7-24-23
   2.  Provided direction to exempt pending applications for self-storage and then adopted
  by a 4/5 vote:

  Ordinance No. O2M23-4816: An Urgency Ordinance of the City Council
  of the City of Alhambra, California, enacted pursuant to California
  Government Code Section 65858, placing a temporary moratorium on the
  issuance of permits or entitlements for any self-storage project in the City

  This ordinance went into effect immediately for a period of 35 days, and a public
  hearing would be scheduled for the Council’s August 28, 2023 meeting to consider
  whether or not to extend the term of the ordinance.

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  MAZA, PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

PUBLIC HEARINGS

6.  PROPOSED WATER RATE INCREASE AND ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION R2M23-40 –
  F2M23-50, R2M23-40

  Director of Public Works & Utilities RAY delivered a staff report. This is the time and place set
  by Notice for the City Council to hold a public hearing to consider a proposed water rate
  increase and adoption of Resolution No. R2M23-40. On May 22, 2023 City Council was
  presented with the Water Rate Study 2023. To ensure that the City can properly fund the
  operation and management of its water system, the City engaged Robert D. Niehaus Inc to
  evaluate the City’s water system revenue needs and calculate a water rate structure that
  proportionally recovers water service costs from its customers. The Water Rate Study 2023
  evaluated the City’s increased costs of service and assessed the adequacy of its existing
  revenues in order to calculate rates to proportionally recover the City’s cost of service from
  each customer level. Water rates have not been increased since 2013. The majority of the
  City’s customers (86 percent) have 5/8” or 1” meters. The median use for all retail customers
  is 9.5 hundred cubic feet (hcf) per month, or 19 hcf per billing period. Under the new rate
  schedule, in the first year, customers with a 5/8” meter who use the median amount of water
  will see an increase of $5.32 per month, or $10.63 per billing period. Customers using the
  median amount of water with a 1” meter will see a $3.33 per month increase, or $7.65 per
  billing period.

  In accordance with Article XIIID of the California Constitution (Proposition 218), notices of this
  public hearing were mailed to every customer and property owner in order to allow the
  community to submit formal protests and/or offer testimony on the proposed water rate
  increase. If a majority of the customers subject to the water rate submit written protests to the
  proposed charges, the Council cannot adopt the resolution, per the requirements of
  Proposition 218. A total of 14,164 notices of the Proposed Increase of Water Rates, printed in
  English, Spanish, and Chinese, were mailed to water system customers. The notice was also
  posted on the City’s website, and made available at City Hall and the Customer Service
  Center. Thus far, 27 letters of protest have been received. Copies of all letters of protest are
  on file at the City Clerk’s Office.

  Opened Public Hearing: Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER opened the public hearing.

  Public Comment:

  5
7-24-23

  3)  Lewis McCammon

  6)  Sharon
  7)  Jennifer

  Closed Public Hearing:  After receiving public testimony, Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER
  closed the public hearing.

  Discussion: Councilmember PÉREZ inquired what water funds are used for, when the last
  time the City increased the water rates, and the availability of the water rate study to the public.
  City Manager BINNQUIST responded to questions.

  Councilmember PÉREZ inquired about the City’s water rates compared to other surrounding
  communities and discussed the impacts to low-income and fixed-income rate payers. Anthony
  Elowsky, RDN, responded to questions.

  Councilmember MALONEY noted that the water fund is to ensure that the City has a safe and
  secure water supply and noted that an increase of the rates is necessary.

  Councilmember LEE discussed the City’s costs to maintain the City’s water infrastructure and
  Director of Public Works and Utilities RAY responded to questions.

  Vice Mayor MAZA discussed the potential deficit of the water fund and the rising costs overall
  and noted that an increase is necessary right now.

  Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER thanked staff for their work on the water rebate program and
  discussed the importance of a safe water supply and maintaining the City’s water
  infrastructure.

  Action Taken:  The City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M23-40 entitled: A
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of Alhambra fixing the rates for water service effective
  July 25, 2023 relating to the adoption of an increase in water rates; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  MAZA, PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER

7.  AMENDED PLAN FOR USE OF AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT OF 2021 RELIEF FUNDS
  – F2M21-67, M2M23-114

  The City Council last amended the City’s American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Plan to add three

  6
7-24-23
   projects to the approved listing. The projects included the purchase of cardiac defibrillators,
  Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) battery backup system, and funding for Almansor Court
  Improvements. City staff have been actively working on the approved list of ARPA projects.
  Cost savings from completed projects, closure of projects that had not begun, and alternative
  grant funding sources are used to fund active projects that require additional funding due to
  price increases. Staff is requesting to add one new project to the Amended ARPA Plan and
  transfer funding to the Premium Pay category. Staff is requesting the City Council approve an
  appropriation from ARPA to fund these projects: 1) The Parks & Recreation Department is
  requesting to reallocate ARPA funds in the amount of $430,000 to repair and resurface pool
  decks to comply with health and safety codes.; 2) The City is proposing to transfer funding for
  the dog park from the Government Services category to Negative Economic Impacts category
  for reporting purposes. The funding is still available for the dog park.; and, 3) The City is
  proposing to reallocate projects that had not begun from the Public Health category to the
  Premium Pay category in the amount of $1,200,000 to provide premium pay benefit to
  essential workers.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council, by one motion, approved the amended American Rescue
  Plan Funds (ARPA) plan as outlined in the Director of Finance’s July 24, 2023 report;
  authorized the Finance Director to amend the ARPA budget for all approved ARPA funds and
  utilize savings to offset overages within current or backup ARPA projects; and, directed staff
  to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M23-114)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MAZA

8.  AUTHORIZE RFP: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING DESIGN SERVICES FOR THE
  GREEN STREET DEMONSTRATION STORMWATER CAPTURE PROJECT ON MAIN
  STREET – F2M23-56, RFP2M23-21

  The proposed Green Street Demonstration Stormwater Capture Project is identified as a
  priority concept in the City’s Stormwater Master Plan. The Project is a first of its kind within
  the City of Alhambra and will provide multiple benefits to the neighborhood and the surrounding
  environment while also reducing stormwater runoff volumes and pollutant loads to receiving
  waters. The Project will also beautify Main Street; comply with water quality regulations;
  enhance open space, include California native drought tolerant plantings and habitat; and
  demonstrate to the public the benefits of green infrastructure.

  Public Comment:  None

  Discussion: Councilmember MALONEY stated he wanted to ensure that the RFP not
  preclude the possibility of a bike lane.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized the distribution of a Request for Proposals to
  qualified firms for Professional Engineering Design Services for the Green Street
  Demonstration Stormwater Capture Project on Main Street; and, directed staff to undertake
  the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

 9.  AWARD CONTRACT: WELL NO. 12 PUMP REPLACEMENT – F2M23-57, C2M23-56,
  M2M23-115

  Well No. 12 is a critical producer of potable water for the City. The well produces approximately
  500 gallons per minute; production that is vital to maintaining an adequate water supply for
  the City. In December of 2022, Well No.12 experienced a shaft issue that required the pump
  to be pulled out of the ground. Staff solicited bids from qualified vendors, with only two
  responding. Tri County Pump was the low bid to pull and inspect the pump. The pump that
  was pulled is 14 years old; upon inspection it was determined the pump, shaft, and column
  piping need to be replaced.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to Tri County Pump for the Well No. 12 Pump
  Replacement in an amount not to exceed $103,663.80; directed the Finance Director to carry
  over the remaining $142,282.00 balance of account 401.80.8884.90837 from Fiscal Year
  2022-2023 to the 2023-2024 Fiscal Year Budget; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-115)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  MAZA, PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

10.  AWARD CONTRACT: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING DESIGN SERVICES FOR THE FY
  2023-2024 SB1 STREET REHABILITATION PROJECT – F2M23-38, RFP2M23-16,
  C2M23-57, M2M23-116

  On May 8, 2023, the City Council authorized staff to circulate a Request for Proposals (RFP)
  for Professional Engineering Design Service for the FY 2023-2024 SB1 Street Rehabilitation
  Project. Staff circulated a RFP and received proposals from five companies. Staff reviewed
  and evaluated the responding proposals and found the proposal submitted by NCE conforms
  to the RFP and received the highest rating. This contract is for the preparation of plans,
  specifications, and cost estimates for the FY 2023-2024 SB1 Street Rehabilitation Project.
  Once the plans are complete, a request for Notice Inviting Bids for the construction phase of
  the project will be presented to City Council for consideration.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to NCE in the amount of $264,430.00 for the Professional
  Engineering Design Services for Plans, Specifications and Cost Estimate for the FY 2023-2024
  SB1 Street Rehabilitation Project; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-116)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  MAZA, PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

11.  AWARD CONTRACT: EMERGENCY PUMP REPAIR AT WELL NO. 13 – F2M23-58,
  C2M23-58, M2M23-117
  8
7-24-23
   Well No. 13 is a non-potable water production well, located at the corner of New and Adams.
  It pumps water directly to the lake at Almansor Park Golf Course to supply water for irrigation
  of the golf course. The well produces approximately 800 gallons per minute of non-potable
  water, thus allowing the City to reserve our potable water supply. After the pump at Well No.
  13 failed, staff contacted General Pump Company, who was available to pull the pump
  immediately. The pump is over 15 years old and after it was removed by General Pump
  Company, an inspection revealed the pump had failed due to bearing wear. Since the pump
  will now need to be completely replaced, it is cost effective to redesign the pump to reduce
  power consumption for a more economical and efficient operation.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to General Pump Company for the Emergency Pump
  Repair at Well No.13 in an amount not to exceed $ $122,829.13; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-117)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  MAZA, PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

12.  RESOLUTION: AUTHORIZE CITY MANAGER TO ACCEPT ON CITY’S BEHALF
  CALTRANS HIGHWAY SAFETY IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM FUNDS – F2M23-18, R2M23-
  35

  The City of Alhambra has been notified the Installation of Pedestrian Countdown Signal Head
  Systems Project submitted under HSIP has been approved in the amount of $876,000. The
  Federal Funds for the Project will be distributed through the California Department of

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M23-35 entitled: A Resolution
  of the Alhambra City Council authorizing the City Manager to act on behalf of the City of

  Ayes:  MAZA, PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

13.  CONFIRMATION OF INTENT TO PARTICIPATE IN THE 2024 GOLDEN STREETS
  MISSION TO MISSION CICLOVIA EVENT – F2M23-16, M2M23-118

  The City has been an active participant in 626 Golden Streets event. To ensure the City’s
  involvement in the new cycle in 2024, the SGVCOG requested a letter of grant support by
  9
7-24-23
   August 18, 2023. The letter indicates that if the grant application for a 626 Golden Streets is
  awarded, the City will support the event’s implementation. It is unclear, however, how much
  funding will be available from the grant source. In the event the City’s costs exceed the grant
  funds available, the City is expected to be responsible for the difference of its share of the
  event costs. Once events are awarded and scheduled, the partner cities will enter into a
  Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the SGVCOG to memorialize the partnership and
  to establish the budget allocated to the cities. The anticipated expenses to participate in the
  next 626 Golden Streets in 2024 is approximately $40,000 with potentially $25,000 to $32,000
  available in reimbursement, depending on the grant received by the SGVCOG. Staff will submit
  these estimates to the SGVCOG, as requested, to assist in their development of the grant
  proposal.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council confirmed the City’s intent to participate in the 626 Golden
  Streets Mission to Mission Ciclovia event; authorized the City Manager, or her designee, to
  execute the Memorandum of Understanding between the cities and the San Gabriel Valley
  Council of Governments to share resources and host the event, if grant funds are received;
  and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-118)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  MAZA, PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

14.  STRATEGIC PLAN UPDATE – F2M23-35

  The 2023 Strategic Plan contains six Goals, defined: Goal 1: Enhance Public Safety; Goal 2:
  Improve Infrastructure and Mobility; Goal 3: Create a Strong Financial Base and Strong
  Economic Base (Economic Development); Goal 4: Enhance Transparency and Open
  Governance; Goal 5: Promote Sustainability; and, Goal 6: Improve Housing Opportunities.
  Staff is now and will continue to present quarterly updates to the Council and will diligently
  work through Strategic Plan goals and individual items to enable important progress.

  Public Comment:

  1) Lewis McCammon, 105 Cordova St., discussed the goals to increase housing
  opportunities in the City, discussed building affordable housing on religious sites, and
  discussed the expiring covenants and noted the City needs to be proactive in this area.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the Alhambra Strategic Plan update.

7-24-23

  authorize rates each fiscal year; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize
  Council’s action. (M2M23-119)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  MAZA, PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

16.  AWARD CONTRACT & APPROPRIATE FUNDS: UNINTERRUPTABLE POWER SUPPLY
  SYSTEMS – F2M23-48, RFP2M23-14, C2M23-60, M2M23-120

  On May 22, 2023, the City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals (RFP)

  THE COUNTY – F2M15-49, F2M23-7, O2M23-4814, M2M23-127
  21
7-24-23
   At the May 8, 2023 City Council meeting, Mayor Andrade-Stadler requested staff research the
  number of permittable dogs and cats per residence. Currently, Alhambra residents are
  permitted to have two dogs and four cats, per Municipal Code Section 7.04.030. The City of
  Alhambra, however, partners with the Los Angeles County Department of Animal Care and
  Control under a City-County Municipal Services Agreement for various animal control
  functions. The limitations under the Los Angeles County Department of Animal Care and
  Control Title 10 - Animals, Section 10.20.038 – Residential Dogs and Cats – Limitations specify
  the following: “A. Dogs. It is unlawful to keep more than four dogs at any residence without an
  animal facility license. Each dog must be licensed. For purposes of this section, a service dog
  licensed under Section 10.20.090 and serving a person who is disabled within the meaning of
  Government Code section 12926 subsection (i) or (j) is not counted toward the number of dogs
  kept or maintained. B. Cats. It is unlawful to keep more than five cats at any residence without
  an animal facility license. Each cat must be licensed and kept primarily indoors.” Based on the
  City’s intent to align residential cat and dog limitations with the County’s Animal Code
  Ordinance (ACO), staff is recommending striking those provisions (Section 7.040.030 (B))
  currently in the City’s Municipal Code and incorporating by reference the County’s limits of
  five cats and four dogs. In addition, staff is recommending amending the contract currently
  underway between the City of Alhambra and the Los Angeles County Department of Animal
  Care and Control to reflect the new limits.

  Public Comment:

  1) Alexander Skinner, 2409 Charwood Ave, expressed support to increasing the pet limits in
  the City.

  Discussion:  Councilmember PÉREZ expressed support to increasing the pet limits in the
  City.

  Councilmember MALONEY noted it makes sense to align with the County Ordinance on pet
  limits.

  Action Taken:  City Council, by one motion, took the following actions:

  1.  Declared introduced for its first reading the following ordinance entitled:
  Ordinance No. O2M23-4814: An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of
  Alhambra updating Chapter 7.04, Section 7.04.030(B), of the Alhambra
  Municipal Code by deleting language pertaining to the number of residential dogs
  and cats and incorporating by reference the higher limits for residential dogs and
  cats allowed by the County

  which ordinance would return for a second reading and adoption at the next Council
  meeting.

  2.  Authorized the City Manager or Designee to amend the City’s contract with the Los
  Angeles County Department of Animal Care and Control for the purposes of
  establishing the new limits of five cats and four dogs. (M2M23-127)

  On June 26, 2023, the City Council conducted a public hearing to consider the disposition of
  real property, a Lot Line Adjustment, General Plan Amendment, and Zone Change for the
  landlocked, unimproved real property approximately 0.29 acres, or 12,937 square feet, in size
  that is part of Story Park (the “Property”) (APN: 5337-002-900) but is separated from the
  improved portion of Story Park by a concrete channel known as the San Pascual Wash. After
  receiving public testimony and deliberation, the Council voted unanimously to adopt several
  resolutions to effectuate the disposition of the real property as well as to approve a Lot Line
  Adjustment (LLA) and General Plan Amendment (GPA). The LLA transfers the approximately
  0.29 acres of landlocked, unimproved real property at Story Park to each of the six abutting
  private residential properties to the east. The GPA changes the General Plan land use
  designation of the transferred land from Open Space to Low Density Residential. The Council
  also voted to give first reading to Ordinance No. O2M23-4813 that changes the zoning
  designation of the transferred land from OS (Open Space) to R-1 (Single-Family Residential).
  Staff requests that the City Council declare this ordinance introduced for its second reading
  and adopt the ordinance.
